artists.biography:
The Stone Roses are an English rock band formed in Manchester in 1983. They were one of the pioneering groups of the Madchester movement that was active during the late 1980s and early 1990s. The band's most successful lineup consists of vocalist Ian Brown, guitarist John Squire, bassist Mani, and drummer Reni.
The band released their debut album, The Stone Roses, in 1989. The album was a breakthrough success for the band and garnered critical acclaim, with many critics regarding it as one of the greatest British albums ever recorded. At this time the group decided to capitalise on their success by signing to a major label. Their current record label, Silvertone, would not let them out of their contract, which led to a long legal battle that culminated with the band signing with Geffen Records in 1991. The Stone Roses then released their second album, Second Coming, which was met with lacklustre reviews in 1994. The group soon disbanded after several lineup changes throughout the supporting tour, which began with Reni first departing in late 1995, followed by Squire in April 1996. Brown and Mani dissolved the remains of the group in October 1996 following their appearance at the Reading Festival.
Following much intensified media speculation, The Stone Roses called a press conference on 18 October 2011 to announce that the band had reunited and would perform a reunion tour of the world in 2012, including three homecoming shows in Heaton Park, Manchester. Plans to record a third album in the future were also floated. In June 2012, Chris Coghill, the writer of the new film which is set during the Stone Roses 1990 Spike Island show, revealed that the band "have at least three or four new tracks recorded". In June 2013, a documentary about the band's reformation directed by Shane Meadows and titled The Stone Roses: Made of Stone was released.

perplexity.description:
The Very Best Of The Stone Roses" is a compilation album released in 1992 by The Stone Roses on Silvertone Records, a division of Sony Music. The album gathers the band's most iconic singles and key tracks from their early career, spanning their influential debut era. Musically, it showcases the band's signature blend of jangly guitar pop, psychedelic rock, and danceable rhythms, which helped define the Madchester scene of the late 1980s and early 1990s. The collection highlights the group's ability to merge melodic songwriting with a distinctive, groove-driven sound, featuring tracks such as "She Bangs the Drums," "Fools Gold," and "Waterfall."

As a retrospective release, "The Very Best Of The Stone Roses" serves as an accessible introduction to the band's discography, capturing their peak creative period before their later, more experimental work. The album was well-received commercially, consolidating the band's status as one of the leading acts of the British indie rock movement. Critics praised the compilation for its cohesive selection and enduring influence, cementing The Stone Roses' legacy as pioneers of a genre that bridged rock and dance music.
